findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the swap comparison correctly distinguishes the running vs published build — compareSemverFull makes the -next tail load-bearing across TWO independently-bumped sources: SELF_VERSION (bootstrapper/package.json, the packageVersion in decideAction) vs the running server's app.version (server/package.json via /api/diagnostics). Staged verbatim, server/package.json carried the committed release triple (no -next.N), so successive @next builds reported the SAME app.version and the stale server was ATTACHED to instead of swapped; and the readiness poll (=== 0) could false-fail even on a successful swap.
Claim under doubt: a republished @next always swaps — The fix keys off a differing version string; a same-version-string republish (same bytes bumped or not) compares === 0 -> attach.
Claim under doubt: every stale incumbent is now swappable — An incumbent reporting app.version 'unknown' (predates version-shipping / garbled) yields compareSemverFull -> 0 -> attach, never swap.
